FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 26 February 1990 after 
the draft finalized by the Jute Mills Machinery/ Accessories and Spare Parts Sectional Committee 
had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 

This standard is intended to provide guidance to the manufacturers of heart cams for jute spinning 
frames. This would ensure the manufacture of heart cams of acceptable quality leading to 
improvement in efficiency and productivity of spinning frames. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS ; 2-1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values {revised y. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that 
of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 12886 : 1990 



Indian Standard 



HEART CAM FOR JUTE SPINNING 
FRAME — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies requirements for 
heart cams for jute spinning frame. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are 
necessary adjuncts to this standard: 



IS No. 
1586 : 1968 

2062 : 1984 

2500 

(Part 1 ) : 1973 

3 MATERIAL 



Title 

Methods for Rockwell hard- 
ness test ( B and G scales ) for 
steel {first revision ) 

Specification for weldable 
structural steel ( third revision ) 

Sampling inspection tables: 
Part 1 Inspection by count of 
defects {first revision ) 



3.1 The heart cam shall be manufactured 
from 14*3 mm thick mild steel plates and the 
steel shall conform to IS 2062 : 1984. 

4 MANUFACTURE 

4.1 The heart cam shall be case hardened to a 
case depth of 1 mm. The heart cam shall be 
symmetrical about the vertical central line 
( see Fig. 1 ). 

5 REQUIREMENTS 

5,1 Dimensions 

The dimensions of the heart cam shall be as 
agreed to between the manufacturer and the 
purchaser or in the absence of any agreement 
the nominal dimensions shall be as declared by 
the manufacturer. 



5.1.1 Tolerances 

The nominal dimensions of the heart cam ( see 
Fig. 1 ) shall be subjected to the following 
tolerances: 



Dimensions 


Tolerance ( in mm ) 


A 


±0-13 


B 


±0-05 


C 


±0-05 


D 


±0'13 


5.2 Hardness 





5,2-1 The heart cam shall have hardness of 
minimum 55 HRG. 

5.2,2 Hardness shall be determined according 
to the method prescribed in IS 1586 : 1968. 

6 MARKING 

6.1 Each heart cam shall be legibly marked with 
the indication of the source of manufacture. 

6.1.1 The heart cam may also be marked with 
the Standard Mark. 

7 PACKING 

7.1 The heart cams shall be packed to ensure 
complete protection from rust. 

8 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 

8.1 To ascertain the conformity of the heart 
cam for jute spinning frame to the requirements 
of this specification, single sampling plan with 
Inspection Level I and Acceptance Quality 
Level ( AQL ) of 1*5 percent given in Tables 1 
and 2 of IS 2500 (Part 1 ) : 1973 shall be 
followed, unless otherwise agreed to between 
the purchaser the manufacturer. 



IS 12886: 1990

All dimensions in millimetres.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is goveriaed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with 
the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked 
products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safe- 
guard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted 
to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards, 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS if a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act^ 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification 
of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), 
BIS.
